title: Retire-and-replace can elect a successor daemon before the retiring writer releases its lease (daemon_writer_unavailable window)
outcome: Retire-and-replace can elect a successor daemon before the retiring writer releases its lease (daemon_writer_unavailable window)
acceptance: A product test proves that after DaemonRetirement.RetireOlderAsync returns, a successor DaemonServer acquires writer ownership on its first attempt while the retiring daemon's IndexManager.Dispose defers ReleaseOwnedResources past its return; WaitForRelinquishmentAsync no longer returns on endpoint disappearance while the retiring generation still holds the lease

completion.summary: Committed a7a9b24: retire-and-replace now waits until the workspace writer lease is provably free before starting a successor; indeterminate lease probes surface the distinct retryable daemon_writer_lease_unverifiable cause; takeover timeout mapping and lifecycle documentation/tests are aligned. The exact reviewed 10-path commit also hardens the contended full-suite Git wrapper test using the existing test-side process ceiling without changing the product timeout.
